notes: US dietary supplement (adults + kids 2-13) sold D2C, with Meta + Google ads. FDA (DSHEA) and FTC rules apply. (1) No disease claims: nothing that says or implies the product will diagnose, treat, cure, mitigate or prevent a disease or symptom-disease (IBS, constipation, colds/flu, hair loss, deficiency disease). Structure/function wording only ('supports digestion', 'supports immune health'), and any page or post that makes one carries the FDA disclaimer below. (2) Never 'FDA approved', 'FDA certified' or 'FDA endorsed'. 'Made in FDA-registered, cGMP-compliant facilities' is fine and is what gruns.co says. (3) No weight-loss or fat-loss promises, no before/after bodies, no body-shaming. GLP-1 content only in third person and as nutrition support ('nutrition for people on GLP-1 medication'). Never name the drugs (Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound), never 'natural GLP-1', never 'replaces your medication'. Weight-related ads are targeted 18+ only. (4) Meta personal-attributes policy: no copy that asserts or implies the viewer's health, medication, pregnancy, age or body ('Do you suffer from…', 'Are you tired of…', 'Coming off your GLP-1?', 'Trying to conceive?', 'your bloating'). Speak about situations in the third person or first person ('I tried both'). (5) Kids line: the audience is parents 18+. Never target or address minors. Never call the product candy, never say 'eat as many as you want'. The kids label carries an iron-overdose warning, so it is one pack per day. Licensed characters (Shrek, Minions) are used only inside the license terms and never in child-directed placements (CARU). (6) Testimonials and endorsers: verbatim only, with written consent for paid use. Show typical experiences only. Extreme outcomes stay out of ads (Wendy B. '15 years', Susan U. 'chronic IBS', Sarah 'fewer stomach issues'). Disclose material connections: creators use Paid partnership + #ad, Shaun White is a paid spokesperson and investor, and gruns.co already says testimonials may be compensated. (7) Numbers: survey stats must say 'in a post-purchase survey of 3k+ customers'. The RCT shows higher blood levels of folate and vitamin C only, so never write 'clinically proven to work'. The '90% of adults' stat comes from a source about vitamins D and E only (PMC9710417), so it must be qualified. (8) gruns.co carries a California Prop 65 lead warning, so never say 'lead-free', 'no heavy metals' or 'zero contaminants'. (9) Offers (FTC + state auto-renewal laws): state the recurring price next to any intro price ($29.99 first order, then $49.99 every 4 weeks). 'Up to X% off' only when X is really available. Deadlines and 'no restocks' must be true. 'Free gifts' must be free. The subscription must say 'pause or cancel anytime' and how. (10) 'Made in the USA' alone is not allowed. The site says USA and Canada, with ingredients sourced globally. Edit freely. 're:' entries are case-insensitive Python regexes.
